title: Bind model-specific replay, dynamic tools, provider search evidence, and billing corrections to UNIIMENTE's canonical control plane
problem: Anthropic released an agent-oriented model with breaking thinking, tool, replay, and computer-use contracts plus dynamic inline and MCP tools; Kimi launched standalone search APIs while scheduling its legacy search tool for retirement; OpenAI introduced key-creation controls and reported Agent API container overbilling and broad API errors. These changes can silently alter authority, replay, evidence, cost, and runtime boundaries.
baseline: Kernel main at 04b1b7e3 owns constitutional authority and canonical state but still lacks a merged provider-change section; draft PR 105 contains the bounded protocol. DALEOBANKS main at e2f1ebed has the only provider runtime found, using OpenAI Chat Completions and optional embeddings with deterministic fallbacks; WMI and PumpStation defer constitutional authority to the Kernel.

alternatives.name: Update the existing draft with narrow new invariants
alternatives.description: Add dynamic-tool manifest, search-evidence, and append-only billing-adjustment rules to draft PR 105 and attach this dated evidence packet; change no runtime.
advantages: Closes genuinely new authority, replay, evidence, and cost ambiguities
disadvantages: Adds review load to an undecided draft
Provider prose still requires future fixtures
alternatives.revival_evidence: Retain while the material findings are not covered by a merged canonical rule.

alternatives.name: Brief only
alternatives.description: Report the provider changes without modifying the existing draft.
disadvantages: Dynamic provider tool manifests and search authority metadata remain implicit
alternatives.revival_evidence: Revive after PR 105 is rejected, simplified, or superseded by an equivalent merged contract.

alternatives.name: Immediate provider migrations
alternatives.description: Adopt Claude Opus 5.5, Kimi search, Agent API containers, or Compliance transcripts now.
advantages: Immediate access to stronger model, dynamic tools, retrieval, and hosted execution
disadvantages: Credential, privacy, cost, and duplicate-runtime exposure
alternatives.revival_evidence: Only founder approval plus adapter fixtures, independent evaluation, data review, cost ceiling, and a singular-runtime proof could revive adoption.

alternatives.name: Fixture-only adapter experiment
alternatives.description: Model Opus 5.5 blocks, dynamic tool manifests, Kimi result/error shapes, provider IDs, and billing corrections inside the existing test system without provider calls.
advantages: Can falsify mappings without credentials or effects
disadvantages: Does not prove live provider behavior
alternatives.revival_evidence: Run only when an owning adapter is proposed and separately authorized.

do_nothing_option.expected_outcome: Current runtime remains safe from direct adoption, but future contributors can misread provider-ranked search as evidence, dynamic tool listings as grants, or refunds as permission to rewrite cost history.
disadvantages: Kimi's October 20 legacy deadline is not durably recorded

roles.position: Preserve access to stronger models, broad tools, retrieval, and computer use while keeping Alfonso's authority, the Consequence Gate, and the single Kernel runtime unchanged.
material_concerns: Vendor features must not narrow the capability horizon
New capability must not manufacture authority

roles.position: Map exact model, thinking lineage, effective tool manifest, retrieval artifacts, diagnostics IDs, receipts, and billing adjustments into existing canonical records.
Provider authority scores, fetched tool listings, status recovery, invoices, and refunds are self-reported claims that can launder evidence, capability, completion, or cost.
material_concerns: Recurring protocol edits becoming de facto policy
evidence_refs: Kimi Web Search Pro response fields

roles.position: DALEOBANKS' current OpenAI draft and embedding paths already degrade to deterministic fallbacks; no model or tool migration is justified by the inspected code.
material_concerns: Emergency key provisioning can be blocked
New compatibility daemon would duplicate operations

roles.position: Treat search content, Chrome transcripts, thinking blocks, and provider evaluations as scoped artifacts with untrusted content and explicit privacy, provenance, retention, and independent-review requirements.

evidence.claim: Claude Opus 5.5 and inline/MCP tool-definition changes were released on 2026-09-22 with material request, response, replay, tool, and pricing differences.
evidence.finding: Thinking cannot be disabled, forced tool choice fails, thinking replay is model-bound, computer-use compatibility differs by platform, and dynamic tool definitions/listings can enter mid-conversation.

evidence.claim: Kimi's September changelog exposes standalone Basic/Pro search and fetch APIs and its pricing page schedules legacy $web_search retirement for 2026-10-20.
evidence.finding: Standalone calls have explicit result/error/diagnostic contracts and per-successful-nonempty pricing; provider authority rankings are returned as metadata.

evidence.claim: OpenAI added new-key creation governance on 2026-09-15, had broad API errors on 2026-09-17, and reported Agent API hosted-container overbilling on 2026-09-18 to 2026-09-19.
evidence.finding: Existing keys were unaffected; Chat Completions and Embeddings were among affected APIs; container usage required mitigation and refund review.

evidence.claim: Only DALEOBANKS has a direct provider runtime surface on the four current default branches.
evidence.reference: GitHub connector reads and searches at 04b1b7e3, e2f1ebed, ec82b802, and db6758df
evidence.finding: No Anthropic, Kimi, Agents API, inline-tool, MCP-client, or relevant model tokens were found; DALEOBANKS uses OpenAI Chat Completions and optional embeddings with deterministic fallbacks.

counterevidence.claim: The new releases require immediate runtime migration.
counterevidence.finding: No owning Anthropic, Kimi, or Agents API adapter exists, and DALEOBANKS' current OpenAI path is bounded to drafts or embeddings with deterministic fallback.

counterevidence.claim: Provider status, authority scores, MCP listings, or refunds prove canonical correctness.
counterevidence.reference: Official provider release, API, pricing, and status pages
counterevidence.finding: The pages define provider behavior and claims but do not establish UNIIMENTE authorization, independent source truth, receipt reconciliation, or local integration behavior.

pass_1.intended_outcome: Keep broad multi-model, retrieval, dynamic-tool, and computer-use capability available while preserving one canonical authority, event, replay, evidence, receipt, cost, and runtime plane.

advantages.statement: Opus 5.5, dynamic tools, and Kimi search expand useful replaceable capabilities.
advantages.amplified_value: Behind canonical adapters they can improve long-horizon work and evidence retrieval without vendor lock-in.

advantages.statement: Provider diagnostics, compliance transcripts, and billing adjustments improve observability.
advantages.amplified_value: Reconciled as subordinate evidence, they can expose replay gaps, privacy failures, and cost discrepancies.

disadvantages.statement: Dynamic tool definitions and MCP listings can silently expand effective capability and authority.
disadvantages.redesigned_response: Hash and preserve the effective manifest, require canonical registry identity and grant checks, and reject unapproved tools before invocation.

disadvantages.statement: Model-bound thinking, forced-tool changes, and platform-specific computer use can break replay or unsafe fallback.
disadvantages.redesigned_response: Preserve raw blocks and exact model/tool contracts; prove cross-model and edited-history behavior with deterministic fixtures before routing.

disadvantages.statement: Kimi authority rankings and retrieved chunks can be mistaken for canonical evidence or evaluator judgment.
disadvantages.redesigned_response: Treat all search content and provider rankings as untrusted evidence metadata; preserve query/source lineage and independently evaluate claims.

disadvantages.statement: Provider usage meters and invoices can be wrong, and refunds can erase historical cost evidence if applied destructively.
disadvantages.redesigned_response: Keep original usage receipts immutable and record refunds or corrections as append-only adjustment events with reconciliation status.

disadvantages.statement: Outages and retries can duplicate calls, spend, work, or external effects.
disadvantages.redesigned_response: Use one canonical attempt/idempotency identity, receipt-gated recovery, bounded retries, circuit breaking, and recovery canaries.

disadvantages.statement: Weekly model-authored updates to an undecided protocol can normalize de facto policy power.
disadvantages.redesigned_response: Keep the PR draft, require founder decision, permit changes only for genuinely material new invariants, and regress after one immaterial update or boundary breach.

comparisons.baseline: Current main has no provider-change section; draft PR 105 already holds the bounded rules and remains unmerged.
comparisons.do_nothing: Avoids churn but leaves dynamic tool, search authority, billing correction, and October 20 legacy retirement semantics implicit.
comparisons.simplest_viable_alternative: Brief-only reporting is simpler but loses durable compatibility and kill rules while a protocol draft already exists.
comparisons.strongest_competing_architecture: Provider-native agent, tool, search, compliance, and billing control planes maximize feature access but fragment authority, replay, evidence, cost, and recovery.
comparisons.reversible_experiment: Offline fixtures can model blocks, manifests, result/error shapes, provider IDs, and adjustments without credentials, live calls, or another scheduler.

rejected_alternatives.name: Immediate adoption
rejected_alternatives.rejection_reason: No direct adapter, authorization, fixture evidence, data review, or singular-runtime proof exists.
rejected_alternatives.revival_evidence: Founder approval plus independently verified adapter fixtures, sandbox canary, cost ceiling, and rollback.

rejected_alternatives.name: Credential or account inventory
rejected_alternatives.rejection_reason: The scheduled review has no authority to inspect policies, keys, contracts, invoices, or balances.
rejected_alternatives.revival_evidence: Separate authorization from the credential/account owner with a least-privilege inspection plan.

rejected_alternatives.name: New compatibility service
rejected_alternatives.rejection_reason: A daemon or provider-session owner would violate the no-duplicate-runtime constraint.
rejected_alternatives.revival_evidence: No revival unless it is demonstrably part of the existing canonical test/runtime substrate and founder approved.

pass_2.attack_summary: The strengthened mapping could still overcollect sensitive transcripts, turn artifact capture into a duplicate evidence store, allow the adapter to bless provider metadata, or accumulate policy without founder judgment.

new_weaknesses.statement: Capturing every provider artifact can duplicate storage and compliance cost.
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: Preserve only authority-, replay-, provenance-, security-, cost-, and debugging-relevant artifacts; use policy-permitted content hashes when full content is unnecessary.

new_weaknesses.statement: A canonical adapter can still silently canonize provider rankings or manifests.
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: Require deterministic acceptance rules and an evaluator independent of the provider/model before promotion.

new_weaknesses.statement: Compatibility fixtures can evolve into a standing scheduler or second runtime.
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: Run fixtures only inside the existing test system; prohibit daemons, queues, provider-owned session managers, and independent retry loops.

new_weaknesses.statement: Materiality language can be stretched to justify endless protocol edits.
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: Tie this update to enumerated new invariants and the October 20 deadline; publish no repository change for an immaterial cycle and preserve dissent.

pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.rationale: The protocol requires exact manifest preservation, canonical registry/grant checks, and rejection before invocation.
pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.review_trigger: Any dynamic tool or MCP adapter proposal

pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.rationale: No adapter exists; deterministic fixtures and independent evaluation are required before migration.
pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.review_trigger: Any Claude Opus 5.5 or computer-use proposal

pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.rationale: Provider ranking is explicitly untrusted evidence metadata and cannot serve as truth, authorization, or sole evaluation.
pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.review_trigger: Any provider search or retrieval adapter proposal

pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.rationale: Original usage receipts remain immutable and adjustments are append-only reconciliation events.
pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.review_trigger: Any provider refund, credit, dispute, or unexplained variance

pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.rationale: Canonical attempt identity, receipt-gated retry, bounded fallback, and canaries govern recovery.
pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.review_trigger: Any timeout, outage, disconnect, or ambiguous completion

pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.rationale: The update is material and remains draft; founder decision and one-immaterial-update kill criteria bound accumulation.
pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.review_trigger: Review of PR 105 or the next weekly cycle

pass_2.final_design: Update existing draft PR 105 only: append the 2026-09-22 review and validated deliberation, and add narrow rules for dynamic tool manifests, provider search evidence, and append-only billing corrections. Make no adapter, model, credential, account, invoice, route, production, authority, or runtime change.

residual_risks.risk: Live account policies, invoices, contracts, and data locations remain unknown.
residual_risks.mitigation: Require separate authorized human inventory before any migration, credential, compliance, or billing action.

residual_risks.risk: One agent performed the five perspectives.
residual_risks.mitigation: Keep the PR draft and require founder or independent human review before merge or adoption.

residual_risks.risk: Provider documentation can mutate in place.
residual_risks.mitigation: Record observation dates, exact endpoints/headers/models, repository commits, and captured fixtures in implementation work.
residual_risks.review_trigger: Next material provider change or adapter proposal

dissent.handling: Preserve the objection in the review and PR. This material docs-only update may proceed reversibly, but merge, provider adoption, account access, and any consequence remain founder decisions.

entries.position: Do not let recurring model-authored protocol edits accumulate indefinitely while PR 105 remains undecided.
entries.rationale: Even accurate edits consume founder attention and can become de facto policy through repetition.
entries.evidence_threshold: Continue repository updates only for a genuinely new invariant, deadline, or direct exposure; otherwise issue a brief only.
entries.review_trigger: Review of PR 105 or one immaterial repository update

migration_plan: No runtime migration. If a provider feature is later proposed, add a narrow canonical adapter contract and deterministic fixtures first; only a separately authorized sandbox canary with independent evaluation, data/retention review, cost ceiling, receipt mapping, and rollback can precede production consideration.

steps: Leave draft PR 105 unmerged or revert its documentation-only commits
Preserve the dated evidence and dissent as historical records
Regress recurring repository edits to brief-only review if the materiality gate fails

kill_criteria: Any write to a default branch or merge without founder approval
Any model, production, credential, account, invoice, contract, or routing change
Any provider-owned canonical workflow, event, authority, memory, evidence, receipt, evaluator, or cost ledger
Any dynamic provider tool installed or invoked without canonical registry and grant checks
Any second scheduler, durable research loop, or agent runtime
Any lost thinking, tool-manifest, search-source, or billing-adjustment lineage
Any missing receipt or duplicate external effect
Any destructive rewrite of original usage or cost history
Any same-provider sole evaluation of promotion or evidence quality
Any unauthorized Compliance API or transcript access
Any ineligible retention or residency path
review_trigger: Founder review of draft PR 105; Kimi legacy search deadline 2026-10-20; any Opus 5.5, dynamic tool, provider search, Compliance API, Agents container, key creation, or provider billing proposal; any ambiguous provider completion
